answer_text:
Let

\[
q=\frac47.
\]

Then the series becomes

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varphi(n)\frac{q^n}{1-q^n}.
\]

Now expand each geometric factor:

\[
\frac{q^n}{1-q^n}=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} q^{nk}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varphi(n)\frac{q^n}{1-q^n}
=
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varphi(n)\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}q^{nk}.
\]

Since \(|q|=4/7<1\), we can rearrange the double sum by grouping terms by the exponent \(m=nk\):

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{n\mid m}\varphi(n)\right)q^m.
\]

Using the standard identity

\[
\sum_{n\mid m}\varphi(n)=m,
\]

we get

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} m q^m.
\]

For \(|q|<1\),

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} m q^m=\frac{q}{(1-q)^2}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\varphi(n)4^n}{7^n-4^n}
=
\frac{\frac47}{\left(1-\frac47\right)^2}
=
\frac{\frac47}{\left(\frac37\right)^2}.
\]

So

\[
\frac{\frac47}{\frac9{49}}
=
\frac47\cdot \frac{49}{9}
=
\frac{28}{9}.
\]

Hence the value of the infinite series is

\[
\boxed{\frac{28}{9}}.
\]
